svg.title: Apple M5 Max compiled localization and selected-attention latency
svg.desc: Dot plot of median latency per synchronized call on Apple M5 Max with MLX 0.32.3, on one zero-based 0 to 400 microsecond scale. Each row joins compiled compositional MLX (hollow gray dot) and the compiled custom Metal kernel (filled blue dot). The first 9 rows are localization at selection widths 128, 2,048, 4,096 and batch sizes 1, 8, 32; Metal is 1.10 to 1.21 times faster. The last 2 rows are complete selected attention with two logical shards on one device, fixed caches and 64-dimensional keys and values: batch 1 with width 128, 1.12 times; batch 8 with width 2,048, 1.12 times. The right-hand column gives each ratio, compiled MLX latency divided by compiled Metal latency. Values are medians of three process-session medians and include dispatch, allocation, execution and synchronization; warmup and first-use compilation are excluded. Compiled Metal was faster in all 33 session pairs; per-session ratios range from 1.10 to 1.77 for localization because one of three sessions ran slower for both arms. Source: evidence/09-apple-mlx-consumer/summary.json, consumer-summary.json and the session records.
